comments.body: When a queue exists you set active_source to queue.queue_id, but MA convention for “MA queue active” is to use player_id (see music_assistant/models/player.py:1955-1961); this makes queue resume logic in PlaybackHandler.play() skip the queue path.

Catching Exception here logs and then silently continues, which can hide real bugs and violates the project’s guidance to avoid broad exceptions and swallowed errors (e.g. https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3096#discussion_r2768368356 and https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/1214#discussion_r1557137671). This PR introduces a new player provider with substantial behavior (discovery, grouping, playback, state sync) but adds no tests; there are existing provider tests under tests/providers/ (e.g. tests/providers/airplay/test_player.py), so adding at least a small unit/integration test surface for the mapping and discovery parsing would help prevent regressions.

await_state_change() swallows TimeoutError, so select_source() can return “success” even when the source never changed (and it also prevents retry_command() from retrying on timeouts). Let the TimeoutError propagate so retries/failures work as intended.

comments.body: If parsing the playlist fails, `playlist` is never assigned, but the function still does `return playlist`, which will raise `UnboundLocalError`. Either return directly from the `try` block or raise a consistent parsing error.
In `_parse_album`, the artist lookup is awaited twice (`await self._client.get_artist(...)` in both the condition and the true branch), causing two network calls for the same data.

Within this provider, `Artist.provider` is set to `self.domain` in `_parse_artist`, but the special-cased "Various Artists" created in `_parse_album` uses `provider=self.instance_id`. This inconsistency can lead to mismatched provider identifiers for artist items coming from the same provider.

`track.duration` is assigned `track_obj["length"]` after checking `str(...).isdigit()`. If the API returns a numeric string, this sets `duration` to a `str` rather than an `int`, which can break consumers expecting a number.
`get_artist_albums` appends the coroutine returned by `_parse_album` instead of awaiting it, so this returns `list[Coroutine]` rather than `list[Album]`.

`handle_async_init` creates an `aiohttp.ClientSession` inside an `async with` block and stores an `IBroadcastClient` that references that session. When the context manager exits, the session is closed, so subsequent provider calls will fail with "Session is closed"-style errors.

Prefer using the long-lived `mass.http_session` (as other providers do) or keep your own session as an instance attribute and close it in `unload()`.

The PR description indicates this is only a benchmark repro for music-assistant/server#1799 and "Safe to close", but this change set adds a new iBroadcast provider (new provider package requirement and provider implementation files). Please update the PR title/description to match the actual scope, or move these provider changes to a dedicated PR.

comments.body: [PROBLEM] handle_async_init creates a new aiohttp ClientSession in an async context manager, which closes at the end of the method; that will break all subsequent API calls made by IBroadcastClient. Music Assistant providers should also reuse the shared session (self.mass.http_session) instead of creating their own (see https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/1817#discussion_r1903244819).

get_artist_albums appends the coroutine returned by _parse_album instead of the parsed Album, because _parse_album is async but isn’t awaited. This will return a list of coroutine objects and likely break callers.

The PR description says this is a benchmark/repro “safe to close”, but this change adds a new runtime dependency (ibroadcastaio) and a full new provider implementation. Please update the PR description to match the intent/scope, or move the provider work into its own PR so it’s reviewable/trackable.

get_playlist swallows parse errors and then returns `playlist`, which is undefined if an exception occurs (UnboundLocalError). Also, per MA guidelines, avoid swallowing errors; raise a typed exception instead (see e.g. https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/1214#discussion_r1557137671).

_parse_album calls self._client.get_artist(album_obj["artist_id"]) twice, which doubles network/API work per album. At minimum, fetch once and reuse the result. Longer-term, consider keeping parsers IO-free and moving lookups out of parsing (see https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2472#discussion_r2400974607).

[PROBLEM] Private helper methods (_get_artist_item_mapping/_get_item_mapping) are defined in the middle of the class, with public methods below them. The project enforces ordering public/dunder methods first and private helpers at the bottom (see https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/4015#discussion_r3428284831).

_get_tracks fetches and parses each track sequentially (await in a for-loop). For playlists/albums with many tracks this can be very slow and becomes an N+1 pattern against the upstream API; consider batching via a bulk endpoint if available or using bounded concurrency (asyncio.gather + semaphore) (see https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3171#discussion_r2813508549).

_parse_track performs API lookups (get_artist/get_album) while parsing. This turns library listings into an N+1 set of network calls and also violates the MA guideline that parsers should be lightweight and IO-free (see https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2472#discussion_r2400974607 and https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/2501#discussion_r2429740886). Consider moving these lookups to the calling methods (with caching) and keeping parsing purely on the provided track payload.

There are provider-level tests in this repo (e.g. tests/providers/jellyfin/*) but this new provider has no tests for its parsing/mapping logic. Adding snapshot/fixture-based tests for album/artist/track parsing would help prevent regressions and clarify expected behavior.
